goal: Measure a representative launcher-plus-core runnable loop without changing the production release profile.

probePolicy: Start every arm from a successful no-op build in its own target directory.
Apply one byte-controlled source replacement and verify exactly one match.
Record source hash, target size, binary hashes, Cargo JSONL, stderr, and cargo-timing HTML.
Restore the original bytes and timestamp, rebuild once to reconcile the target, and require a clean nested repository status.
Do not compare arms while another build owns the same target directory.

arms.codegenUnits: Cargo dev default; confirm from verbose rustc argv before implementation
arms.panic: Cargo dev default unwind; confirm from verbose rustc argv before implementation
arms.purpose: Best low-conflict hypothesis for a warm runnable edit loop.
Isolate the benefit and storage cost of incremental compiler state.
Measure cold/fresh-target reuse versus changed-core misses without mixing incremental state.
protocol: Allocate a dedicated SCCACHE_DIR and SCCACHE_SERVER_PORT so the arm neither reuses nor stops another build's server.
Start from an empty cache directory and record zeroed advanced statistics.
Build target C1 from cold to seed the isolated cache.
Build a second fresh target C2 against the same isolated cache to measure cross-target reuse.
Apply the controlled core probe in C2 to measure changed-core hit, miss, non-cacheable, and error deltas.
Stop only the isolated-port server and retain before/after advanced statistics with the Cargo evidence.

arms.purpose: Quantify symbol and disk overhead only when source-level debugging is required.
Trade compile/link time against runtime responsiveness only if opt-level 0 proves unusably slow.

fixedDecisions: LTO-on is not a development candidate; it is already the release/publish fidelity gate.
panic=abort is rejected because it changes failure semantics from both the current dev and release profiles.
A direct codex-core-only command is a lower-bound diagnostic, not the representative runnable artifact.
The representative command keeps the launcher adjacent to codex-core because the launcher owns provider flags, bootstrap, policy, and environment setup.
A globally shared target is rejected; concurrent worktrees require separate targets and explicit ownership locking.
comparisonMetrics: warm no-op wall seconds and rebuilt package count
target bytes and incremental subdirectory bytes
launcher and core bytes plus SHA-256
first and repeated process startup latency
stopRule: Once one additive arm produces a representative changed-core launcher-path run in at most 600 seconds without weakening release gates, defer more expensive optimization sweeps unless their expected value exceeds another full cold target warm-up.
